{"id": "e8d2a538-e64b-4c68-9d90-de60a4118d74", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Why are my Lambda functions in eu-central-1 slow on the first request after a quiet period?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "c0dd267a-1e54-42f3-be98-5288c2d78d7a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This is the classic **Lambda cold start** pattern — here's what's happening:

**Why it happens:**
- Lambda spins down idle execution environments after a period of inactivity (roughly 15–60+ min depending on load patterns, not officially fixed).
- The next invocation after that has to spin up a brand-new environment: pull your code/image, start the runtime, and run any top-level/init code (SDK clients, DB connections, config loading, etc.) before your handler even runs.
- That setup overhead shows up as added latency on just the first request — subsequent requests reuse the warm environment and are fast again.

**What makes it worse:**
- **Runtime** — Java and .NET typically have noticeably longer init times than Python or Node.js.
- **Package/image size** — larger deployment packages or container images take longer to load.
- **VPC-attached functions** — ENI setup used to be a major cold-start tax; AWS improved this significantly, but it can still add some latency depending on config.
- **Heavy init code** — loading large dependencies, establishing DB/connection-pool clients, or fetching secrets/config at startup all run during the cold path.

**Common fixes:**
- **Provisioned Concurrency** — keeps a pool of environments pre-initialized and warm.
- **SnapStart** (Java, and now some other runtimes) — snapshots an initialized environment to skip most of the init cost.
- Trim package size, lazy-load non-critical dependencies, move expensive init work out of the hot path where possible.
- For scheduled low-traffic functions, a lightweight periodic "ping" can keep one environment warm, though Provisioned Concurrency is the more reliable approach.

Want me to pull actual init-duration metrics or recent invocation data for your specific eu-central-1 functions to confirm this is what's driving the slowness and see how big the impact is?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
